english: Good morning! How are you?
grammar: Apa kabar? is literally 'what news?' — the everyday 'how are you?'. Reply: Kabar baik.

english: Good day, Mrs. Sari.
grammar: Bu (short for Ibu) is the polite title for a woman: Selamat siang, Bu Sari.

english: Good afternoon, Mr. Budi.
Good evening, everyone.
I'm fine, thank you.
Hello, nice to meet you.
grammar: bertemu = ber- + temu (meet): Senang bertemu dengan kamu = nice to meet you.

english: See you tomorrow!
Goodbye, sir.
grammar: Selamat tinggal is a final goodbye; for 'see you later' say Sampai jumpa.

english: Welcome to our house.
How is your family?
My name is Andi.
grammar: Indonesian drops 'is' in simple sentences: Nama saya Andi = My name (is) Andi.

english: What is your name?
I am from England.
Where do you live?
grammar: di mana = where; question words often sit at the end: Kamu tinggal di mana?

english: I live in Jakarta.
Let me introduce you, this is my wife.
grammar: Perkenalkan opens an introduction: Perkenalkan, ini istri saya = meet my wife.

english: Pleased to make your acquaintance.
I work at a hospital.
grammar: bekerja = ber- + kerja (work): Saya bekerja di rumah sakit = I work at a hospital.

english: He is my friend from the office.
This is my business card.
I am an English teacher.
grammar: No word for 'am/is' before nouns: Saya guru = I am a teacher.

english: You are a new student, right?
Mr. Budi is our manager.
He is my younger sibling.
grammar: In conversation just drop 'is': Dia adik saya. adalah sounds formal, like a definition.

english: We are from Australia.
We are friends now.
grammar: kita includes the listener, kami excludes them: kita pergi (you too) / kami pergi (not you).

english: They are tourists from Japan.
Indonesian is the national language.
We live together in Bandung.
They came from Surabaya.
This is my parents' house.
grammar: ini before a noun = 'this is'; after it = 'this': ini rumah (this is a house) / rumah ini (this house).

english: That is the post office.
This is my passport.
That is our hotel.
This is my husband, his name is Tono.
Those are their children.
Thank you very much, sir!
You're welcome, ma'am.
grammar: Sama-sama ('same-same') is the standard reply to terima kasih.

english: Excuse me, I want to get past.
Sorry, I arrived late.
I am not hungry now.
grammar: tidak negates verbs/adjectives, bukan negates nouns: Saya tidak lapar. / Ini bukan rumah saya.

english: He does not like coffee.
We do not have a car.
This is not my bag.
He is not a teacher, he is a doctor.
grammar: bukan can correct a noun: Dia bukan guru, dia dokter = not a teacher but a doctor.

english: That is not a big problem.
I am not Japanese.
They are not working today.
That child does not want to sleep.
This house is not big.
My mother is not from Bali.
This coffee is not hot.
I do not know that road.
That is not my room key.

target: Kami bukan turis, kami tinggal di sini.
english: We are not tourists, we live here.
I cannot come tomorrow.
grammar: bisa = can: Saya tidak bisa datang = I cannot come.

english: He does not drink tea.
Do you like spicy food?
grammar: Apakah turns a statement into a yes/no question: Kamu suka kopi. → Apakah kamu suka kopi?

english: Are there still any rooms available?
Is she your older sibling?

target: Apakah bus ini pergi ke bandara?
english: Does this bus go to the airport?
Can you help me?
grammar: membantu = mem- + bantu (help); meN- makes the active verb.

english: Is the office open on Saturday?
Is this the train to Bogor?
Have you eaten yet?
grammar: sudah = already: Apakah kamu sudah makan? = Have you eaten (yet)?

english: Are you Indonesian?
grammar: In speech a rising tone alone makes a yes/no question: Kamu orang Indonesia?

english: Is he coming tomorrow?
Is this my seat?
Do you work here?
What is that, sir?
What do you want to drink?
grammar: apa can sit at the end: Kamu mau minum apa? = What do you want to drink?

english: What is the name of this street?
What is your child's name?
grammar: Asking a name uses siapa (who), not apa: Siapa nama kamu? = What is your name?

english: Who is that at the front door?
Who is your manager at the office?

target: Saya sudah makan siang di kantor.
english: I already ate lunch at the office.
grammar: sudah marks completion — no past tense needed: Saya sudah makan. (I already ate.)

english: We have already arrived at the hotel.

target: Ibu sudah bangun sejak jam lima pagi.
english: Mom has been up since five in the morning.

target: Dia sudah selesai bekerja hari ini.
english: He has already finished working today.
Have you already had coffee?
grammar: Answer a sudah question with the marker itself: Sudah. (Already.) or Belum. (Not yet.)

english: The children are already asleep in the bedroom.
The train has already arrived at the station.
I have not had breakfast yet this morning.
grammar: belum = not yet — expected to happen later: Saya belum makan. (I have not eaten yet.)

english: Dad has not come home from the office yet.
We have not bought the plane tickets yet.
She has not finished washing the dishes yet.
You're not asleep yet?

target: Saya belum menerima jawaban dari mereka.
english: I have not received an answer from them yet.
Mom is cooking in the kitchen.
grammar: sedang marks action in progress: Ibu sedang memasak. (Mom is cooking right now.)

target: Saya sedang menunggu bus di halte.
english: I am waiting for the bus at the stop.
They are having dinner together.

target: Adik sedang belajar untuk ujian besok.
english: My younger sibling is studying for tomorrow's exam.
grammar: untuk = for (purpose): belajar untuk ujian (study for the exam)

english: We are working on a new project.
He is speaking with a guest.

target: Saya akan pergi ke pasar besok pagi.
english: I will go to the market tomorrow morning.
grammar: akan marks the future — the verb never changes: Saya akan pergi. (I will go.)

target: Kami akan datang ke rumah kamu nanti malam.
english: We will come to your house tonight.

target: Dia akan mulai pekerjaan baru bulan depan.
english: She will start a new job next month.
The plane will arrive shortly.

target: Saya akan membayar dengan uang tunai.
english: I will pay with cash.

target: Mereka akan menjual rumah itu tahun depan.
english: They will sell that house next year.
I just woke up.
grammar: baru saja = just now: Saya baru saja bangun. (I just woke up.)

english: That guest just left.

target: Kami baru saja selesai makan malam.
english: We just finished dinner.

target: Bus ke bandara baru saja berangkat.
english: The bus to the airport just left.

target: Dia baru saja mengirim email itu.
english: He just sent that email.

target: Saya masih menunggu di depan toko.
english: I am still waiting in front of the store.
Dad is still working at the office.
grammar: masih = still, the action continues: Dia masih bekerja. (He is still working.)

english: This coffee is still hot.

target: Kami masih punya waktu satu jam.
english: We still have one hour.
That store is still open now.

target: Saya pernah pergi ke Bali dua kali.
english: I have been to Bali twice.
grammar: pernah = have ever done at least once: Saya pernah ke Bali. (I have been to Bali.)

english: Have you ever eaten satay?
He has never been on a plane.
grammar: belum pernah = never so far: Dia belum pernah naik pesawat. (He has never flown.)

english: We once lived in Jakarta.

target: Ibu pernah bekerja di rumah sakit.
english: Mom once worked at a hospital.
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
grammar: di mana asks where something is: Di mana kamar mandi? (Where is the bathroom?)

english: Where do you live now?

target: Ke mana kamu pergi hari ini?
english: Where are you going today?
grammar: ke mana asks where to (motion): Ke mana kamu pergi? (Where are you going?)

english: Where does this bus go?
grammar: Destination questions can drop the verb: Bus ini ke mana? (Where does this bus go?)

english: Where is your family from?

target: Dari mana kamu tahu berita itu?
english: Where did you hear that news from?
When are you going home?
grammar: kapan = when: Kapan kamu pulang? (When are you going home?)

english: When does this store open again?
When will we meet again?

target: Kapan kamu mulai kerja di kantor baru?
english: When do you start work at the new office?
How much is this ticket?
grammar: berapa asks how much or how many: Berapa harga tiket ini? (How much is this ticket?)

target: Harga tiket masuk lima puluh ribu rupiah.
english: The entrance ticket costs fifty thousand rupiah.
grammar: Tens stack simply: lima puluh = five tens = 50, dua puluh = 20.

target: Kopi ini harganya dua puluh lima ribu.
english: This coffee costs twenty-five thousand.
How many people are in your family?

target: Ada empat orang di keluarga saya.
english: There are four people in my family.
grammar: ada = there is/are: Ada empat orang. (There are four people.)

target: Saya mau beli tiga kilo beras.
english: I want to buy three kilos of rice.
grammar: After mau, the bare root is natural in speech: mau beli = want to buy.

english: How old is your child now?
grammar: berapa umur = how old: Berapa umur anak kamu? (How old is your child?)

target: Umur saya tiga puluh dua tahun.
english: I am thirty-two years old.

target: Kamar ini seratus ribu rupiah semalam.
english: This room is one hundred thousand rupiah a night.
grammar: se- means one: seratus = one hundred, semalam = one night.

target: Kami butuh dua kamar untuk empat orang.
english: We need two rooms for four people.
What time is it there now?
grammar: jam berapa = what time: Jam berapa sekarang? (What time is it now?)

english: It is nine in the morning now.
grammar: Time of day follows the hour: jam sembilan pagi = 9 a.m., jam sembilan malam = 9 p.m.

target: Jam berapa kamu bangun setiap pagi?
english: What time do you wake up every morning?

target: Saya mulai kerja jam delapan pagi.
english: I start work at eight in the morning.

target: Kereta ke Bandung datang jam tiga sore.
english: The train to Bandung arrives at three in the afternoon.
grammar: sore = late afternoon, about 3-6 p.m.: jam tiga sore = 3 p.m.

english: We eat dinner at seven o'clock.

target: Pasar buka dari pagi sampai sore.
english: The market is open from morning until late afternoon.

target: Siang ini saya makan di rumah.
english: This afternoon I am eating at home.
How is your family doing?
grammar: bagaimana = how: Bagaimana kabar kamu? (How are you?)

english: How do I get to the station?

target: Bagaimana cuaca di Jakarta hari ini?
english: How is the weather in Jakarta today?
Today is Monday, isn't it?
grammar: Days take hari first: hari Senin = Monday, hari Sabtu = Saturday.

target: Kami pergi ke pantai hari Sabtu.
english: We are going to the beach on Saturday.
I do not work on Sunday.

target: Rapat itu hari Jumat jam sepuluh pagi.
english: The meeting is on Friday at ten in the morning.
I wake up early every day.

target: Dia mencuci muka di kamar mandi.
english: She washes her face in the bathroom.
grammar: Before c, meN- becomes men-: cuci → mencuci (wash).

target: Ibu memasak nasi goreng untuk sarapan.
english: Mom cooks fried rice for breakfast.
grammar: Roots starting with m keep a simple me-: masak → memasak (cook).

english: We have breakfast together in the kitchen.

target: Saya menulis catatan di buku kecil.
english: I write notes in a small book.
grammar: Before t, meN- becomes men- and the t drops: tulis → menulis (write).

english: Dad reads the newspaper every morning.
grammar: Before b, meN- becomes mem- and the b stays: baca → membaca (read).

english: I buy coffee before working.

target: Dia bekerja di kantor sampai sore.
english: He works at the office until late afternoon.

target: Kakak menonton televisi setelah makan malam.
english: My older sibling watches television after dinner.
I sleep at ten at night.

target: Setiap pagi saya mandi air dingin.
english: Every morning I bathe with cold water.
She sweeps the floor before leaving.
grammar: Before s, meN- becomes meny- and the s drops: sapu → menyapu (sweep).

english: I take a towel from the cupboard.
grammar: Vowel-first roots take meng-: ambil → mengambil (take).

target: Ibu mencuci baju setiap hari Sabtu.
english: Mom washes clothes every Saturday.
I am reading a new book.
grammar: sedang marks an action happening right now: sedang membaca = is reading.

english: My younger sibling writes a letter to a friend.
We cook dinner together.

target: Saya minum teh hangat pagi ini.
english: I drink warm tea this morning.

target: Dia sudah bangun sebelum matahari terbit.
english: He already woke up before sunrise.
grammar: sudah marks a finished action: sudah bangun = already woke up.

english: I close the window before sleeping.
grammar: sebelum (before) takes a verb directly: sebelum tidur = before sleeping.

target: Ayah membuka toko jam delapan pagi.
english: Dad opens the shop at eight in the morning.
I listen to music while cooking.
grammar: sambil = while (one person, two actions): makan sambil membaca = eat while reading.

english: After work I go straight home.
grammar: langsung means straight away: langsung pulang = go straight home.

target: Kakak sedang mencuci piring di dapur.
english: My older sibling is washing dishes in the kitchen.

target: Saya memakai baju kerja setiap hari Senin.
english: I wear work clothes every Monday.
She brings packed food to the office.

target: Saya menonton berita sebelum berangkat kerja.
english: I watch the news before leaving for work.
The children study after lunch.

target: Saya mengirim pesan ke teman kerja.
english: I send a message to a coworker.

target: Ibu membangunkan adik jam enam pagi.
english: Mom wakes my younger sibling at six in the morning.
grammar: -kan makes a verb act on someone: bangun (wake up) → membangunkan (wake someone up).

target: Saya menulis daftar belanja untuk besok.
english: I write a shopping list for tomorrow.

target: Dia membacakan cerita untuk anaknya setiap malam.
english: She reads her child a story every night.
grammar: -kan can mean doing it for someone: membaca (read) → membacakan (read aloud to someone).

target: Kami membersihkan rumah di akhir pekan.
english: We clean the house on the weekend.

target: Saya mulai bekerja jam sembilan pagi.
english: I start work at nine in the morning.
Dad turns off the lamp before sleeping.
I have bread and eggs for breakfast.

target: Dia sedang menulis laporan untuk kantor.
english: He is writing a report for the office.
I wash my hands before eating.

target: Setiap malam saya membaca sebelum tidur.
english: Every night I read before sleeping.

target: Kami tidur lebih awal di hari kerja.
english: We sleep earlier on workdays.

target: Saya mau pesan nasi goreng satu.
english: I want to order one fried rice.
grammar: mau + verb = want to: mau pesan = want to order.

target: Makanan di warung ini enak sekali.
english: The food at this food stall is very tasty.
Please do not make it too spicy.
I want to try chicken satay.
Just sweet iced tea to drink.
grammar: saja means just/only: es teh saja = just iced tea.

target: Berapa harga satu porsi mie goreng?
english: How much is one portion of fried noodles?
grammar: Berapa harga ...? asks a price: Berapa harga kopi ini? = How much is this coffee?

english: Is this food spicy?

target: Saya pesan ayam goreng dan nasi putih.
english: I order fried chicken and white rice.
May I have plain water?
grammar: Boleh minta ...? politely asks for something: Boleh minta air? = May I have water?

english: It tastes sweet and a little spicy.
grammar: -nya can mean the/its: rasa (taste) → rasanya (the taste of it).

target: Kami makan malam di restoran dekat hotel.
english: We have dinner at a restaurant near the hotel.
May I see the menu again?
I like Indonesian food.
The waiter brings our order.
The food has arrived, please eat.
grammar: silakan politely invites someone to act: silakan makan = please eat.

target: Saya mau membeli oleh-oleh untuk keluarga.
english: I want to buy souvenirs for my family.
How much is this bag?

target: Wah, itu terlalu mahal untuk saya.
english: Wow, that is too expensive for me.
grammar: terlalu = too (more than you want): terlalu mahal = too expensive.

english: Can the price come down a little?
If I buy two, is there a discount?
grammar: kalau means if: kalau beli dua = if (you) buy two.

english: This shirt is cheap and nice.

target: Saya membeli buah di pasar pagi.
english: I buy fruit at the morning market.

target: Penjual itu memberi saya harga khusus.
english: That seller gives me a special price.
I pay with cash.
Is there a bigger size?
grammar: yang turns a description into the one that: yang lebih besar = the bigger one.

english: That shop is closed on Sundays.
I am looking for sandals for the beach.
Prices at the market can be bargained.
grammar: di- makes a verb passive: tawar (bargain) → ditawar (be bargained over).

target: Dia menjual kain batik yang cantik.
english: She sells beautiful batik cloth.

target: Saya coba dulu baju ini, ya?
english: Let me try this shirt first, okay?
grammar: dulu after a verb means first: coba dulu = try it first.

english: Thank you, just keep the change.

target: Kami membeli air minum di toko kecil.
english: We buy drinking water at a small shop.
My order has not come yet.

target: Kopi di sini lebih murah daripada di hotel.
english: Coffee here is cheaper than at the hotel.
grammar: lebih ... daripada compares: lebih murah daripada di hotel = cheaper than at the hotel.

english: I am full, the food is very tasty.

target: Saya punya dua kakak dan satu adik.
english: I have two older siblings and one younger sibling.
grammar: punya = have: Saya punya adik = I have a younger sibling.

target: Ibu saya suka memasak di rumah.
english: My mother likes to cook at home.
grammar: Possessor comes AFTER the noun: ibu saya = my mother (lit. mother I).

target: Ayah saya bekerja di kantor besar.
english: My father works at a big office.
My older sibling lives in Bandung.
My younger sibling is still small.
My house is near the market.
Her child is already big now.
My husband likes black coffee.
His wife is Balinese.
My friend's name is Sari.
Our family lives in Jakarta.
grammar: kami = we (not you); kita = we (with you): keluarga kami = our family.

english: His mother is sleeping in the bedroom.
grammar: -nya on a noun = his/her: ibunya = his/her mother.

english: His house is big and clean.
grammar: No word for 'is' before adjectives: Rumahnya besar = His house (is) big.

target: Dia suka bermain bola dengan temannya.
english: He likes playing football with his friend.

target: Kakek dan nenek saya tinggal di desa.
english: My grandfather and grandmother live in a village.

target: Dia punya banyak teman di sekolah.
english: She has many friends at school.
My friend is very kind.
That person is tall and thin.
Has your younger sibling eaten yet?
grammar: sudah ... belum? = already or not yet: Sudah makan belum? = Eaten yet?

english: I love my family.
We have one daughter.
grammar: anak perempuan = daughter (lit. child female); anak laki-laki = son.

english: That boy is my son.

target: Ibu saya lebih muda dari ayah saya.
english: My mother is younger than my father.
grammar: lebih + adjective + dari = more ... than: lebih muda dari = younger than.

english: My older sibling got married last year.
Her husband works at a hospital.
My grandmother is good at cooking rendang.

target: Anak-anak sedang bermain di depan rumah.
english: The children are playing in front of the house.
grammar: Doubling a noun makes it plural: anak-anak = children.

english: How old are you now?
My younger sibling is ten years old.

target: Orang tua saya tinggal jauh dari sini.
english: My parents live far from here.
grammar: orang tua = parents (lit. old people): orang tua saya = my parents.

english: He is the first child in his family.
My teacher is a patient person.

target: Teman saya datang dari Surabaya kemarin.
english: My friend came from Surabaya yesterday.

target: Mereka punya rumah baru di kota.
english: They have a new house in the city.
People here are very friendly.
My wife is an English teacher.
grammar: No word for is: Istri saya guru = My wife (is) a teacher.

target: Saya tinggal dengan orang tua saya.
english: I live with my parents.

target: Keluarga besar kami berkumpul setiap tahun.
english: Our extended family gathers every year.
grammar: keluarga besar = extended family (lit. big family).

target: Belok kiri di lampu merah itu.
english: Turn left at that traffic light.
grammar: belok kiri = turn left; belok kanan = turn right.

target: Kantor pos ada di sebelah kanan.
english: The post office is on the right side.
Keep going straight until the market.
That hotel is near the beach.
My office is far from home.
grammar: jauh dari = far from; dekat dengan = near to.

target: Saya naik bus ke kantor setiap hari.
english: I take the bus to the office every day.
grammar: naik + vehicle = take/ride: naik bus = take the bus.

target: Dia naik kereta ke Bogor pagi ini.
english: She takes the train to Bogor this morning.

target: Kami naik ojek karena jalan macet.
english: We took a motorcycle taxi because the road was jammed.

target: Tas saya ada di atas meja.
english: My bag is on the table.
grammar: di + position word: di atas meja = on (top of) the table.

target: Kucing itu tidur di bawah kursi.
english: That cat is sleeping under the chair.

target: Kunci ada di dalam tas hitam itu.
english: The key is inside that black bag.

target: Mobil saya parkir di depan gedung.
english: My car is parked in front of the building.
grammar: di depan = in front of; di belakang = behind.

target: Toilet ada di belakang ruang rapat.
english: The toilet is behind the meeting room.

target: Saya bekerja di kantor dekat stasiun.
english: I work at an office near the station.
The meeting starts at nine in the morning.

target: Bos saya sedang rapat dengan klien.
english: My boss is in a meeting with a client.

target: Saya berangkat ke kantor jam tujuh.
english: I leave for the office at seven.

target: Dari sini ke bandara berapa lama?
english: How long from here to the airport?
grammar: dari ... ke ... = from ... to: dari sini ke bandara = from here to the airport.

target: Naik taksi ke bandara mahal sekali.
english: Taking a taxi to the airport is very expensive.
Where is the nearest bus stop?
grammar: ter- + adjective = the most: terdekat = the nearest, from dekat (near).

target: Halte bus ada di depan bank.
english: The bus stop is in front of the bank.
I get off at the next stop.
grammar: naik = get on, turun = get off: turun di halte = get off at the stop.

target: Kereta ke Surabaya berangkat jam delapan.
english: The train to Surabaya departs at eight.

target: Maaf, saya datang terlambat ke rapat.
english: Sorry, I came late to the meeting.

target: Kantor kami ada di lantai lima.
english: Our office is on the fifth floor.

target: Saya sudah mengirim email ke bos.
english: I have already sent an email to the boss.

target: Jangan lupa bawa laptop ke rapat.
english: Don't forget to bring a laptop to the meeting.
grammar: jangan = don't (command): Jangan lupa! = Don't forget!

target: Dia sedang bekerja dari rumah hari ini.
english: He is working from home today.

target: Stasiun kereta ada di dekat hotel.
english: The train station is near the hotel.
Turn right after the post office.

target: Saya jalan kaki ke pasar setiap pagi.
english: I walk to the market every morning.
grammar: jalan kaki = go on foot: Saya jalan kaki ke pasar = I walk to the market.

target: Minggu ini saya sangat sibuk dengan pekerjaan.
english: This week I am very busy with work.

target: Ruang rapat ada di sebelah dapur.
english: The meeting room is next to the kitchen.

target: Bus itu berhenti di depan sekolah.
english: That bus stops in front of the school.

target: Saya pulang dari kantor naik kereta.
english: I go home from the office by train.

target: Mereka pergi ke luar kota untuk bekerja.
english: They go out of town for work.

target: Selamat, kamu dapat pekerjaan baru itu!
english: Congratulations, you got that new job!
